newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shui On group unit suspended from HK tender bids.
newsitem.headline: Shui On group unit suspended from HK tender bids.

text.p: Shui On Building Contractors Ltd has been suspended from bidding on tenders for three months after being held responsible for water contamination at two Hong Kong housing estates, a government spokeswoman said on Saturday.
The government earlier issued a statement saying a contractor had been suspended from bidding but did not name the company.
The spokeswoman confirmed it was Shui On Contractors, a unit of the Shui On group and one of the largest builders of public housing in Hong Kong.
The company could not be reached for comment.

"To the contractor, this represents a loss of tendering opportunities for seven sizeable projects involving an estimated tender sum of over HK$4 billion," the statement quoted a Housing Authority spokesman was saying.

The decision to suspend the contractor followed a Housing Department investigation which found Shui On responsible for contaminating water at two public housing estates in Ma On Shan in the New Territories earlier this month, the statement said.
More than 1,000 households were affected, it added.
Local newspapers reported that a faulty connection of pipes at the two housing estates caused flushing water from Tolo Harbour to be piped into residents' homes instead of fresh water.
Some mothers had prepared bottles for their babies using the salt water, the South China Morning Post said.
The contractor had promised to pay the March water bills of the affected residents and to settle bills for the repair of damaged appliances, it said.

Shui On Construction and Materials Ltd was incorporated in Bermuda in January to become the holding company for the group's construction and building materials activities and was listed on the Hong Kong stock exchange in February.
